Anthropic's massive IPO (target $2 trillion valuation) and explosive revenue growth (10x from year-start).
High market liquidity and willingness to invest in high-growth AI companies.

Anthropic's deep technical advantage with advanced AI models and strengthening US military cooperation.

AI engineers are becoming wealthy, with high talent retention in AI companies.
Soaring procurement by AI giants benefits product-selling companies.
Massive and growing procurement by cloud companies (year-end forecast $1.5-$1.6 trillion).
AI infrastructure build-out is unprecedented in scale, largest national-level infrastructure project ever.
AI is progressing through development stages, currently at autonomous planning/execution.
Innovative data collection methods for AI (e.g., Indian laborers with cameras).
AI product sellers are profitable, and OpenAI is generating revenue from subscriptions.
Hollywood is embracing AI, and acceptance of AI-generated content is growing.
AI-assisted content creation (e.g., Chinese short dramas) is successful and generating significant revenue ($9B annually in US).
AI adoption and impact are spreading across diverse industries (e.g., smart garbage trucks, AI legal, AI music).
AI's productivity explosion and spillover effects.
Strong AI development in image/video generation, especially in China.
AI as a tool to enhance human creativity.
High demand for engineers in the market.
AI has spillover effects, new companies, data centers, cost reduction, profit increase.
bearish_points: Muted market reaction to strong Q2 earnings, with tech stocks lagging.
"Buy everything with eyes closed" phase for AI is ending.
Long-term bond yields are not falling despite flat PPI, indicating market concern.
Divergence in AI sector performance, with some areas lagging (memory, AI power).
Market is becoming more cautious in the current rebound.
Significant drop in US semiconductor leveraged ETF (SOXL) and lack of new subscriptions.
Pullbacks in AI supply chain due to leverage build-up, not fundamental weakening.
Tech giants facing pressure from high capital expenditure.
Tencent's market cap being surpassed, indicating a shift away from traditional tech giants.
Market preference is shifting away from traditional tech giants like Tencent.
High borrowing needs but stubbornly high financing costs despite cooling inflation.
Stubbornly high long-term bond yields (30-year US Treasury yield at 5.22%, a new century high) despite cooling inflation, indicating market concern.
Broad-based rise in real yields, government bond yields, and investment-grade bond issuance yields to 25-year highs.
Contradiction between easing inflation and persistently high bond yields.
Bond market is smelling risk earlier than the stock market.
High financing demand is leading to bond selling pressure and higher yields.
Declining free cash flow for cloud giants (peaked at $120B in 2024, now around $30B).
Most tech giants' FCF is declining, with potential cash crunch if major players like Microsoft falter.
Nvidia resorting to financial engineering (turning GPUs into financial assets) to raise funds.
Concerns about the financialization of computing power and its potential to become a real debt market.
Rapid growth of GPU/AI chip-backed debt (from tens of billions in 2023 to $700B in 2026).
Analogy to the subprime mortgage crisis, using AI assets (GPUs, data centers) as collateral for loans.
The speed of financialization is a significant concern.
Risk of financial crisis if the underlying assumptions of AI models suddenly change (similar to 2008 housing crisis).
AI financialization implies rising risk.
Potential tipping point for AI investments around 2028-2029, with uncertainty about free cash flow recovery after data center construction.
Bond market is currently under the most pressure, not the stock market.
Soaring CDS trading volume indicates hedging against financing risks, not necessarily bearish but cautious.
Pressure building in software stocks, which are seeing significant corrections.
Software stocks are facing AI replacement risk, as AI can perform coding tasks cheaper.
Severe losses for private equity in the software sector, indicating broader financial stress.
Deterioration in the tech leveraged loan market, with bond investors worried about repayment ability.
Doubts about software companies' ability to repay debt, turning into a credit issue.
Private equity investments in software face huge pressure.
AI replacing coders, combined with high P/E ratios and existing debt in software, is leading to market pressure.
Software stocks are identified as the worst performers this year.
The software sector's struggles serve as a warning sign for the broader AI financing landscape.
The entire AI game, while propping up a huge economy, carries the risk of significant economic damage if the AI bubble bursts.
The growing reliance of the US economy on AI investment (mega-cap tech capex as % of GDP rapidly expanding) increases systemic risk.
US economic growth is heavily dependent on AI; without it, growth would be less than 1%.
Excessive debt and financialization in AI are negative factors.
The market is potentially over-investing and over-leveraging in AI, pulling future value into present stock prices.
Philosophical questions about the meaning of human work in an AI-dominated future.
Market concerns and skepticism about AI investment.
